items.title: May the Prayer You Need Find You
items.moral: Moral: When you help those in need and show tenderness to the vulnerable, you become worthy of others’ prayers. The kindness you offer today may return to you when you need it most.
body: Be the hand that helps someone out of poverty, the door a person in need can knock on, the kindness that comforts an orphan, the shoes on a child’s bare feet. Bring relief in hard times, so that a prayer may find you when you need one yourself.

items.title: My Alif Has Been Dotted
items.moral: Moral: A single letter—or a single moment—can turn joy into sorrow. Expressions preserve the feelings and stories behind them.
body: There is an expression in Turkish: “elifim noktalandı.” It comes from writing the letters “alif” (ا) and “ha” (ه) side by side in the old Ottoman script (اه). Because the “ha” after “alif” resembles a dot, people say “alifim noktalandı,” and metaphorically it means “my joy turned to sorrow.” The letter “alif,” with its long, thin appearance, expresses freedom and beauty, while the letter “ha,” with its bent, almost crushed appearance, expresses distress and collapse.
Together, the two letters form the sigh “ah.”

items.title: The Same Complaint
items.moral: Moral: Repetition alone changes nothing. Give your energy to finding a way forward.
body: A wise man met a group who kept complaining about the same problems. He told them a joke, and everyone laughed. He repeated it, and only a few smiled. The third time, no one reacted.
Repeating a complaint without seeking a solution can have the same effect. Eventually, people stop listening.

items.title: Choose Your Confidants Carefully
items.moral: Moral: Trust your pain to people who will treat it with care.
body: Not every sorrow should be shared with everyone.
Some people may one day use it to hurt you.
